Background/Aims Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) is prevalent in both economically developed and developing countries. Twenty percent of NASH progresses to cirrhosis with/without hepatocellular carcinoma, and there is an urgent need to find biomarkers for early diagnosis and monitoring progression of the disease. Using immunohistochemical and immunoelectron microscopic examination we previously reported that expression of matrix metalloproteinase-1 (MMP-1) increased in monocytes, Kupffer cells and hepatic stellate cells in early stage NASH. The present study investigated whether serum MMP-1 levels reflect disease activity and pharmaceutical effects in NASH patients. Methods We measured the serum levels of MMPs, tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), and several cytokines/chemokines in patients with histologically proven early and advanced stages of NASH and compared them with those in healthy controls. Results Serum MMP-1 levels in stage 1 fibrosis, but not in the more advanced fibrosis stages, were significantly higher than in healthy controls ( P =0.019). There was no correlation between serum MMP-1 level and fibrosis stage. Serum MMP- 1 levels in NASH patients represented disease activity estimated by serum aminotransferase values during the follow-up period. In contrast, MMP-2, MMP-9 and TIMPs did not change with disease activity. Consistent with the finding that MMP-1 is expressed predominantly in monocytes and Kupffer cells, serum levels of monocyte chemotactic protein-1 and granulocyte-colony stimulating factor were significantly increased in NASH with stage 1 fibrosis. Conclusions These results suggest that serum MMP-1 levels represent disease activity and may serve as a potential biomarker for monitoring the progression of NASH. Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis Matrix metalloprotease 1 Cytokines Liver cirrhosis INTRODUCTION Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) is prevalent in both economically developed and developing countries [ 1 ]. In Japan the number of NASH patients has been rising in recent years [ 2 ]. Most patients with NASH show increased body weight due to over eating and low physical activity, and frequently present with metabolic syndrome and diabetes mellitus [ 3 , 4 ]. Triglyceride deposits in hepatocytes cause oxidative stress in mitochondria, leading to cell death of hepatocytes and inflammation with infiltration of monocytes in the liver [ 3 - 6 ] as well as hepatocellular carcinoma with or without cirrhosis [ 7 ]. If inflammation is not observed, the term nonalcoholic fatty liver (NAFL) is usually used in clinical practice, and the term nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) includes both NASH and NAFL [ 4 ]. Recently we published a report on spatiotemporal expression of matrix metalloproteinase-1 (MMP-1) in histologically proven NASH liver [ 8 ]. Immunohistochemical (IHC) and immunoelectron microscopic (IEM) examination revealed that monocytes (MCs), Kupffer cells (KCs) and hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) were positive for MMP-1 in the early stage of NASH while hepatic progenitor cells (HPC) with MMP-1 expression appeared to transform into both bile ductules participating in ductular reaction and elongated capillary endothelial cells involving angiogenesis in the advanced stage of NASH. MMP-1 positive HPCs were observed even in the early stage of NASH [ 9 ]. MMP-1 is a typical interstitial collagenase, one of the soluble-type MMPs. Moreover, MMP-1 possesses not only the unique function of breakdown of type I collagen at one quarter distance from the N-terminal of the collagen molecule [ 10 ], but also the ability to initiate cell proliferation [ 11 - 13 ] as well as the ability to alter cell phenotype [ 14 ]. We then measured the serum levels of MMP-1 of patients with histologically proven NASH and compared them with those in healthy controls. We measured not only MMP-1 but also other MMPs, tissue inhibitor of metalloproteases (TIMPs), stromal cell-derived factor 1α (SDF-1α), and several cytokines to examine disease activity linked with progression to advanced stage NASH, cirrhosis and HCC [ 8 ]. In the present study we show that the serum level of MMP-1 is unique in reflecting the disease activity compared with the serum levels of other MMPs, their inhibitors and cytokines involved in their activation and discuss the possibility of translational research to inhibit the exosomes from KCs, MCs and HSCs, including miRNA related to MMP-1 expression as a novel target for NASH.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated serum levels of various biomarkers, including matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), cytokines (SDF-1α, SCGF-β, SCF-1, G-CSF, MCP-1), hormones (leptin, ghrelin), and liver enzymes (ALT, AST, γ-GTP), in patients with histologically proven nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The aim was to determine if these biomarkers reflect disease activity, steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis progression across early and advanced NASH stages. The study also evaluated the impact of pharmacological interventions, specifically pioglitazone and ezetimibe, and lifestyle modifications on these biomarkers and the clinical course of NASH. Key findings identified serum MMP-1 as significantly higher in early-stage NASH (stage 1 fibrosis) and reflective of disease activity, while SDF-1α strongly correlated with fibrosis, steatosis, and inflammation across various stages. Pioglitazone treatment was observed to improve histological features and modulate biomarker levels, decreasing MMP-1 and increasing SDF-1α.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease progression and correlation with biomarkers, supplemented by pharmacological interventions and lifestyle modifications.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved both observational components, comparing serum biomarker levels in patients with histologically proven early (n=24) and advanced (n=9) NASH against healthy controls (n=14), with subgroup analysis based on histological characteristics. Pharmacological interventions included pioglitazone, administered at 15 mg daily for durations ranging from over two months to two or more years, and in some cases for 14 months concurrently with ezetimibe. Ezetimibe was also administered alone for 10 months. Other unspecified lipid-lowering and anti-diabetic agents, along with diet and physical activity, were also utilized. While changes before and after treatment were observed, comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported, focusing more on the outcomes of specific treatment regimens.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher than in healthy controls (P=0.019) in stage 1 fibrosis, but did not correlate with more advanced fibrosis stages (F2-F4). Levels represented disease activity estimated by serum aminotransferase values during follow-up and paralleled changes in ALT. Tendency to be higher in early NASH patients compared to advanced NASH and controls (no statistical significance), and in grade 2 steatosis, and grades 1 and 2 inflammation. Decreased gradually after 14 months of pioglitazone and ezetimibe, with lowered levels preceding an ALT decrease in an advanced NASH patient. Decreased in the ALT improved group (without statistical significance) and tended to decrease markedly in F1 NASH patients after pioglitazone for two months. Showed no change or slight decrease in F2 NASH patients after pioglitazone. Lower at 70 weeks in the ALT improved group versus the ALT uncontrolled group (without significance). Showed complex relationships with body weight, ALT, and HbA1c in metabolic syndrome and diabetes patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Typical interstitial collagenase; breaks down type I, II, III collagen; involved in extracellular matrix degradation and tissue remodeling; initiates cell proliferation; alters cell phenotype; activates Kupffer cells (KCs), hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), endothelial cells (ECs), and hepatic progenitor cells (HPCs); involved in early rapid reaction to oxidative stress.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Histologically proven Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), particularly in early stage (stage 1 fibrosis/F1) and reflecting overall disease activity. Also observed after pioglitazone and ezetimibe treatment, in ALT improved/uncontrolled groups, and in NASH patients with metabolic syndrome or diabetes.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Best reflected disease activity in the clinical course of NASH; may serve as a potential biomarker for monitoring NASH progression, particularly useful for early diagnosis. Higher levels may contribute to further NASH progression, while reduction with pioglitazone indicates improvement. Its complex relationship with other metabolic indicators warrants context-specific interpretation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not change with NASH disease activity. Statistically higher in advanced NASH patients compared to early NASH and controls; higher in fibrosis stage 4 (F4 group) compared to healthy controls (P<0.01); tendency to be higher in grade 1 steatosis, grade 3 inflammation, grade 2 ballooning, and F3 group. Some correlation with stages of fibrosis observed (P=0.051). Exhibited no difference before and after pioglitazone administration over two months.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Extracellular matrix degradation; involved in tissue remodeling and fibrosis, particularly type IV collagen.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease activity, advanced NASH, NASH with fibrosis stage 4 (F4), fibrosis stage 3 (F3), grade 1 steatosis, grade 3 inflammation, grade 2 ballooning. Response to pioglitazone treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of advanced NASH and progression of liver fibrosis, particularly severe fibrosis (F4), but did not reflect steatosis or inflammation. Not indicated as a biomarker for general NASH disease activity due to lack of change, and levels are not affected by short-term pioglitazone treatment.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not change with NASH disease activity and did not parallel it. Tendency to be higher in early NASH patients compared to advanced NASH and controls (no statistical significance); tendency to be higher in grade 2 steatosis, grade 2 inflammation, and F1 group (no correlation with histological findings observed). Decreased gradually after 14 months of pioglitazone and ezetimibe. Showed some decrease in the F2 group after pioglitazone administration.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Extracellular matrix degradation; involved in tissue remodeling, particularly type IV collagen; related to grades of steatosis and inflammation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease activity, early NASH, NASH with fibrosis stage 1 (F1), grade 2 steatosis, grade 2 inflammation. After pioglitazone and ezetimibe treatment, F2 NASH group after pioglitazone administration.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Not indicated as a biomarker for general NASH disease activity due to lack of change, but potentially a mild indicator of early NASH and F1. Decreased levels may indicate disease improvement or response to treatment.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not change with NASH disease activity.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Inhibitors of metalloproteinases.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease activity.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Not indicated as a biomarker for NASH disease activity due to lack of change.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not change with NASH disease activity. Higher in advanced NASH patients compared to healthy controls and early NASH patients; significantly higher in fibrosis stage 4 (F4 group) compared to healthy controls (P<0.01); tendency to be higher in grade 2 steatosis, grade 3 inflammation, and grade 2 ballooning. Statistically significant correlation with stages of fibrosis observed (P=0.038). Exhibited no difference before and after pioglitazone administration over two months.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Inhibits matrix metalloproteinase activity; involved in extracellular matrix remodeling and fibrosis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease activity, advanced NASH, NASH with fibrosis stage 4 (F4), grade 2 steatosis, grade 3 inflammation, grade 2 ballooning. Response to pioglitazone treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of advanced NASH and progression of liver fibrosis, particularly severe fibrosis (F4), but did not reflect steatosis or inflammation. Not indicated as a biomarker for general NASH disease activity due to lack of change, and levels are not affected by short-term pioglitazone treatment.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher in advanced NASH patients compared to healthy controls and early NASH patients; slightly higher tendency in grade 3 inflammation and fibrosis stage 4 (F4 group) compared to healthy controls. Exhibited no difference before and after pioglitazone administration over two months.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Inhibits matrix metalloproteinase activity, particularly MMP-2; involved in extracellular matrix remodeling and fibrosis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Advanced NASH, NASH with grade 3 inflammation, fibrosis stage 4 (F4). Response to pioglitazone treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with advanced NASH and severe inflammation or fibrosis, but did not reflect steatosis or inflammation. Levels are not affected by short-term pioglitazone treatment, suggesting it might not be a sensitive short-term indicator of treatment response.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in NASH with stage 1 fibrosis. Higher than in healthy controls with statistical difference (P <0.05 for early NASH and P <0.01 for advanced NASH). Significantly higher for grades 2 and 3 of steatosis, grade 2 of inflammation, grade 2 of ballooning, and the F1 group than in healthy controls. Significantly higher serum levels observed at an early stage, probably the beginning stage of NASH subsequent to steatosis of hepatocytes. Significantly correlated with all grades of histological findings: steatosis (P =0.002), inflammation (P =0.005), ballooning (P =0.001), and fibrosis (P =0.046).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Chemokine that mediates monocyte chemotaxis; recruits monocytes to sites of inflammation; promotes hepatic accumulation of bone marrow-derived CCR2-expressing monocytes (MCs), expanding the local macrophage pool.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Early and advanced Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), particularly with stage 1 fibrosis, grades 2 and 3 of steatosis, grade 2 of inflammation, grade 2 of ballooning, and F1 fibrosis group, reflecting early disease stage and macrophage infiltration.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammatory activity and is a robust biomarker for NASH progression, significantly correlated with all key histological features (steatosis, inflammation, ballooning, fibrosis). Associated with early stage NASH, consistent with MMP-1 expression in monocytes and Kupffer cells, suggesting an indicator of early inflammatory activity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in NASH with stage 1 fibrosis. Statistically higher in early NASH patients. Statistically higher than in healthy controls in grade 2 of inflammation and F3 group. Higher serum levels observed (no statistical difference) in all grades of steatosis, grades 1 and 3 of inflammation, grades 1 and 2 of ballooning, and F1 and F2 groups. The F3 group showed the highest levels, while the F4 group showed the same levels as healthy controls. No correlation with histological findings was observed. May cause increased levels of SDF-1 (based on an acute liver failure model, not directly quantified in NASH patients in this study).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Colony-stimulating factor for granulocytes; involved in hematopoiesis, immune cell mobilization, immune response, inflammation, and cell proliferation. Reported to prevent development of hepatic steatosis (in rat NASH models); enhances SDF-1 gradient inducing chemo-attraction of CD34+ cells from bone marrow to injured liver; reported to activate HSCs, KCs, and ECs in NASH progression.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Early Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), NASH with stage 1 fibrosis, grade 2 inflammation, fibrosis stage 3 (F3), and various other histological grades (all grades steatosis, inflammation grades 1-3, ballooning grades 1-2, fibrosis stages F1-F4). Acute liver failure models and NASH models.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with early stage NASH and specific inflammatory and fibrotic stages (elevated in F3, normal in F4). Its lack of direct correlation with histological findings suggests it may not be a direct progression marker, but it may indicate inflammatory or fibrotic activity in NASH. Potentially has a protective role against hepatic steatosis.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lowered to a normal value of 20 IU/L after 14 months of pioglitazone and ezetimibe. Still high after 10 months of ezetimibe treatment. Values less than 30 IU/L on final observation at 70 weeks for improved group; values ">=30 IU/L at 70 weeks for uncontrolled group. Increased due to overeating, increased body weight, and low physical activity. Tended to decrease in F1 and F2 NASH patients after pioglitazone administration (P =0.225, P =0.074, respectively). Changes in ALT values paralleled serum levels of MMP-1. Significant improvement of ALT with pioglitazone; a similar decrease in serum ALT is expected with pioglitazone treatment.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Liver enzyme, indicative of hepatocellular damage and inflammation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Clinical course of Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) patients, monitoring disease activity and treatment response over 70 weeks. After ezetimibe treatment, after pioglitazone and ezetimibe treatment, associated with overeating, increased body weight, low physical activity, ALT improved group, ALT uncontrolled group, F1 and F2 NASH patients. NASH disease activity.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates liver damage level; disease activity in NASH can be determined to some extent using serum ALT. Improved ALT values suggest therapeutic efficacy and disease improvement, while increased ALT suggests liver damage or worsening disease. Used to classify NASH patients into 'improved' or 'uncontrolled' groups based on treatment response.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically higher in both early and advanced NASH patients compared to controls (P<0.001). Statistically higher by grade of fibrosis (r=0.649, P <0.001), steatosis, and inflammation. Significantly higher in grades 1 and 2 steatosis, grades 2 and 3 inflammation, grades 1 and 2 ballooning, and F2, F3, and F4 groups compared to healthy controls, with the F4 group (clinical liver cirrhosis) having the highest levels. Statistically significant correlations with all histological findings: steatosis (P=0.005), inflammation (P<0.001), ballooning (P=0.002), and fibrosis (P<0.001). Increased after pioglitazone administration (P =0.110) in F1 NASH patients, though not significantly. Showed no change in F2 NASH patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cytokine reported to activate hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), Kupffer cells (KCs), and endothelial cells (ECs) in NASH progression; main regulating factor for trafficking and homing of hematopoietic stem cells; activates HSCs via CXCR4; involved in cell migration, angiogenesis, inflammation and fibrogenesis; secreted by KCs and sinusoidal endothelial cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Early and advanced NASH, NASH with various histological grades (steatosis grades 1-2, inflammation grades 2-3, ballooning grades 1-2, fibrosis stages F2-F4), particularly severe fibrosis (F4/cirrhosis). F1 and F2 NASH patients after pioglitazone administration. Progression of NASH (fibrosis, steatosis, inflammation).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Strong indicator of NASH presence and progression, significantly correlated with all key histological features, especially severe liver fibrosis/cirrhosis. Increase with pioglitazone suggests a beneficial effect in F1 NASH, potentially playing a role in the response to treatment or disease modulation. Potentially a useful biomarker of disease activity and progression.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in advanced NASH patients compared to controls (P=0.001). Tendency to show higher levels in grade 2 steatosis, grades 2 and 3 inflammation, grade 2 ballooning, and F1 and F3 groups. Levels in the F4 group were not high. Significant correlation with steatosis (P=0.025), inflammation (P=0.012), and ballooning (P=0.008). Serum levels appeared related to inflammation and were very similar to SDF-1α, MMP-2, and TIMPs.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cytokine, implied role in cellular activation during NASH progression; involved in proliferation and migration of stem cells and HPCs.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Advanced NASH, NASH with grade 2 steatosis, grades 2-3 inflammation, grade 2 ballooning, fibrosis stages F1 and F3. Progression of NASH, inflammation.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of advanced NASH, correlated with specific histological features (steatosis, inflammation, ballooning), but not necessarily with the most severe fibrosis (F4). Related to inflammation in NASH.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Tendency to be higher in grade 1 steatosis, grades 1 and 3 inflammation, grade 1 ballooning, and F1, F3 and F4 groups. Grade 2 steatosis, grades 1 and 3 inflammation, and F1, F3 and F4 groups showed a slightly higher tendency. No correlation between serum SCF-1 level and grade of histological finding observed. Serum levels appeared related to inflammation; levels were similar to MCP-1, G-CSF, and leptin, and reflected the beginning of steatosis with inflammation.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cytokine reported to activate HSCs, KCs, and ECs in NASH progression; involved in proliferation and migration of stem cells and HPCs.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: NASH with various histological grades (steatosis grades 1-2, inflammation grades 1-3, ballooning grade 1, fibrosis stages F1, F3, F4). Progression of NASH, inflammation, beginning of steatosis.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential indicator across various NASH stages, but without strong statistical correlation with histological findings reported. Related to inflammation and the onset of steatosis in NASH.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in both early and advanced NASH than in healthy controls (P <0.01 and P <0.05, respectively). Elevated with no statistical difference by grade of steatosis and inflammation. Statistically higher levels compared with healthy controls in grade 2 of ballooning and the F1 group. Statistical correlation between serum levels of leptin and grades of steatosis (r=0.505, P <0.001) and inflammation (r=0.483, P <0.002); serum levels were not higher in the F4 group. Significantly correlated with all grades of histological findings (steatosis, inflammation, ballooning, fibrosis; P =0.001, P =0.002, P =0.004 and P =0.038, respectively).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Adipokine involved in appetite regulation, energy balance, metabolism, inflammation, and fibrosis. Related to obesity; reduces development of fibrosis in liver injury models; activates multiple intracellular signaling pathways in HSCs; maintains quiescent state of HSCs by inhibitory activity of PPAR-γ.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Early NASH, advanced NASH, grade 2 of ballooning, F1 fibrosis group, various grades of steatosis and inflammation in NASH.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels indicate NASH presence and are significantly correlated with all grades of histological findings, suggesting it is a robust marker for NASH progression and related to steatosis and inflammation. Its complex role includes potentially maintaining HSC quiescence.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: same as healthy controls, very different
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels were the same as those in healthy controls. Levels were unique for all grades of histological findings, showing an inverse relationship with healthy controls but without statistical difference. The correlation with all grades of histological findings also showed an inverse relationship with no statistical difference. Serum levels were very different from those of the other cytokines (SDF-1α, SCGF-β, SCF-1, MCP-1, G-CSF, leptin); no significant difference in plasma levels reported in NASH patients treated with melatonin (cited study).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Appetite-stimulating hormone, involved in energy homeostasis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) patients, all grades of histological findings (steatosis, inflammation, ballooning, fibrosis).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Levels are not significantly different from healthy controls in NASH and show a non-significant inverse relationship with histological findings, suggesting it may not be a direct indicator for NASH progression. Potentially associated with more severe NAFLD (cited study); important cytokine in NASH requiring further research.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Improved after 14 months of pioglitazone and ezetimibe. Altered due to depression, excess eating, and lowered physical activity.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Liver enzyme, indicator of liver cell damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: After pioglitazone and ezetimibe treatment, associated with depression, excess eating, lowered physical activity.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates liver damage; improvement suggests therapeutic efficacy and disease improvement.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Improved after 14 months of pioglitazone and ezetimibe. Altered due to depression, excess eating, and lowered physical activity.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in glutathione metabolism, often elevated in liver and bile duct diseases.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: After pioglitazone and ezetimibe treatment, associated with depression, excess eating, lowered physical activity.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates liver or bile duct damage; improvement suggests therapeutic efficacy and disease improvement.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Slightly higher levels between 5.8 to 6.6% in five diabetes patients in the ALT uncontrolled group. Not correlated with changing serum MMP-1 and ALT levels. Significant improvement of HbA1c with pioglitazone treatment. Did not effect on serum levels of MMP-1.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicator of average blood glucose levels over the past 2-3 months; marker of long-term blood glucose control.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Diabetes patients in ALT uncontrolled group. Extrahepatic inflammatory conditions in NASH, pioglitazone treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates blood glucose control; higher levels suggest poorer diabetes management. No correlation with MMP-1 or ALT suggests independent regulation in this specific context. Improvement suggests better glycemic control and overall health.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased after ezetimibe treatment. Changing levels were not consistent with serum MMP-1 levels.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol to tissues; high levels are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: After ezetimibe treatment, metabolic syndrome patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates lipid profile; decreased levels suggest improved lipid management. Inconsistent correlation with MMP-1 suggests complex interplay with disease activity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased after ezetimibe treatment. Changing levels were not consistent with serum MMP-1 levels.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Form of fat stored in the body; high levels are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease and metabolic syndrome.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: After ezetimibe treatment, metabolic syndrome patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates lipid profile; decreased levels suggest improved lipid management. Inconsistent correlation with MMP-1 suggests complex interplay with disease activity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The plasma adiponectin level increased with pioglitazone treatment (cited study).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Involved in improving insulin resistance.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Pioglitazone treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Increase indicates improved insulin resistance, potentially contributing to improvement of steatosis, inflammation, and ballooning in NASH.
